SeriesStatAccessor::normr¶

Back to SeriesStatAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series SeriesStatAccessor::normr() const
Series SeriesStatProxy::normr() const

What It Does¶

normr() scales each row to Euclidean length one while preserving shape and direction. For row vector r, it computes r / ||r||_2. A rank-1 input is treated as one vector. An all-zero row remains zero.

This is magnitude normalization, not statistical standardization: it does not subtract a mean, and its output need not have zero mean or unit variance.

Returns And Call Styles¶

The result is an out-of-place floating Series with the owner’s shape. Direct x.stat.normr() and proxy x.stat().normr() spellings are equivalent; no peer is bound for this unary operation.

Examples¶

Example 1. Each row receives its own denominator.

auto x = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 4.0}, {0.0, 5.0}});
std::cout << x.stat.normr() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[0.6, 0.8],
  [0, 1]]

The first row divides by 5; the second also divides by 5. Direction is preserved even though magnitude is removed.

Example 2. Squared row components sum to one after normalization.

std::cout << x.stat().normr().square().sum(1) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 1]

The squared values in each nonzero row sum to one, proving unit L2 length.

Example 3. Zero vectors stay finite but cannot be made unit length.

auto x = pluss::make_series({{0.0, 0.0}, {3.0, 4.0}});
std::cout << x.stat.normr() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[0, 0],
  [0.6, 0.8]]

Gradient Geometry¶

For nonzero r, reverse mode projects sensitivity onto the tangent plane of the unit sphere and divides by ||r||. Changes parallel to r alter magnitude only, so normalization removes that component.

Example 4. Reverse mode includes both the division and the input-dependent row norm.

auto x = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 4.0}, {5.0, 12.0}});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
x.stat.normr().sum().reverse();
std::cout << x.sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[0.032, -0.024],
  [0.038233955, -0.015930815]]

See Also¶

  • normc: normalize columns instead.

  • standardize: center and scale by statistical spread.
